name: Hurghada
title: Holidays in Hurghada
intro: A long Red Sea strip of resorts and sandy beaches, with coral islands offshore and ancient Luxor a day trip away. Here's what Hurghada is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Palm trees silhouetted against an orange sunset over the Red Sea at Hurghada
facts_note: Many hotels are all-inclusive. Check the latest travel advice on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: March to May and September to November are the best times, hot and sunny with a warm sea. Winter is sunny and around 21 to 23°C, though windy at times. July and August are very hot, but a sea breeze helps on the coast.

things.name: Giftun Islands
things.blurb: Boat trips to white-sand islands and coral reefs.

things.name: El Gouna
things.blurb: A lagoon town of canals, beaches and restaurants, 30 minutes north.

things.name: Hurghada Marina
things.blurb: A promenade of cafés and boats, best in the evening.

things.name: Diving and snorkelling
things.blurb: Reefs, dolphins and wrecks, with many dive centres for beginners.

things.name: Luxor
things.blurb: The Valley of the Kings and Karnak Temple, about 4 hours away by road.

things.name: Makadi Bay
things.blurb: A calmer resort area south of town with house reefs.

faqs.question: Is Hurghada good for a beach holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. Most hotels have their own beach, and many have reefs for snorkelling.

faqs.question: Can you visit Luxor from Hurghada?
faqs.answer: Yes, on a long day trip by road, about 4 hours each way, or stay overnight.

faqs.question: Is Hurghada or Sharm el-Sheikh better?
faqs.answer: Sharm has better reefs and mountain scenery. Hurghada is cheaper, with more choice and easy trips to Luxor.
